profile.reading:
This TierPoint facility is located in the Charlotte, North Carolina area, in Mecklenburg County, and carries the internal reference code CL4 in the source map data, which most plausibly signals TierPoint's fourth Charlotte-area building or numbering position, though this could not be independently confirmed against TierPoint's own public materials this session. TierPoint's current website lists two named Charlotte facilities: a North Myers Street location with more than 30,600 total square feet and more than 7,500 square feet of raised floor, and a larger Center Park Drive location with more than 60,000 total square feet and more than 20,000 square feet of raised floor, backed by four 2.25-megawatt redundant generators on what TierPoint describes as the area's second-priority power grid. Neither of TierPoint's own facility pages states an internal "CL" numbering scheme, so this record cannot be confidently matched to one specific building, and rather than guess, this entry is filed against the general Charlotte market context. Both facilities carry TierPoint's standard compliance package of SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II certifications including HITRUST, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GLBA, and ISO 27001. No acquisition history was found tying Charlotte into TierPoint's well-documented roll-up of Xand, Windstream Hosted Solutions, and Cosentry, and Charlotte is notably absent from the states TierPoint listed as active markets in its own December 2015 Windstream acquisition announcement, suggesting the Charlotte presence was established through a later, undocumented transaction. TierPoint, headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri, describes its national footprint as roughly 40 data centers across 20 US markets.

TierPoint has also grown through significant recent capital raises beyond its acquisition history: a 320 million dollar equity round in April 2020 led by Argo Infrastructure Partners, Wafra, and Macquarie Capital Principal Finance alongside existing investors, followed by Argo's 500 million dollar investment in February 2022 that made it TierPoint's largest single equity investor, and a further increase to Argo's ownership and capital commitment announced in December 2025.
profile.research_note: TierPoint operates two named Charlotte-area facilities per its own site: North Myers (125 North Myers St, Charlotte NC 28202, 30,600+ sqft total, 7,500+ raised floor) and Center Park (1805 Center Park Drive, Charlotte NC 28217, 60,000+ sqft total, 20,000+ raised floor). This OSM record carries ref code CL4, which could not be matched with confidence to either named facility from TierPoint's own site (WebSearch quota exhausted, and neither facility page states an internal CL-number designation). Address and specific building-level detail are therefore NOT asserted here to avoid guessing which of the two this record refers to. Both are listed for honest disambiguation. No acquisition history for either Charlotte site was found -- notably, TierPoint's own Dec 2015 Windstream Hosted Solutions press release lists TierPoint's then-current states as WA, TX, OK, PA, MD, NY, MA, CT, and FL, with NC absent, implying the Charlotte presence was added via a later, undocumented deal.

reading.body:
The TierPoint Charlotte Data Center publishes 20,000 square feet of technical space and no IT load figure in megawatts, making its relevance to AI infrastructure scaling impossible to determine from available data.

Certifications alone reveal the facility's role in the data center ecosystem. Six distinct compliance credentials—SOC 1 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, HITRUST, ISO 27001, and ITAR—qualify it for regulated workloads that hyperscale-only campuses often cannot serve. This is infrastructure for financial systems, healthcare data, and defense-controlled information, not the homogeneous compute farms that drive AI model training. The compliance posture indicates a generalist facility serving multiple industries rather than an AI-focused deployment.

North Carolina shows 19 facilities on this registry with only one publishing a megawatt figure—40 MW. The state's near-total lack of disclosed power data obscures actual capacity. A facility cannot be ranked meaningfully by the absence of information. Without a published power number for this campus, no valid comparison to other sites is possible, and no estimate of its racks, accelerators, or role in grid constraints can be made.
